title: Garter square shawl
subtitle: A centre-out DK square in garter stitch — four mitered sections growing from a cast-on corner.
excerpt: A square garter shawl in DK wool, worked from the centre out using a 4-section mitered construction with yarn-over increases at four corner points. Each section is plain garter stitch. Finished size approximately 130 × 130 cm when blocked. About 500 g of DK yarn. An ideal first-centre-out project.
sourceNotes: Centre-out square shawl construction appears in Weldon's Practical Knitter, 2nd series (1886), §Shawls, and in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Square Shawls. The four-section mitered form with yarn-over corners is a standard Victorian construction for square shawls and coverlets.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 44 rows = 10 × 10 cm in garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked.

glossaryTerms.definition: A knitting construction that begins at the centre of a square and grows outward to all four edges. In the garter version, a small cast-on anchors four sections divided by markers; yarn-over increases at each corner create the four-pointed growth.
A corner shaping technique in which increases or decreases are placed symmetrically around a pivot stitch, creating a neat 45-degree angle at the corner point.

The shawl begins with a small central cast-on and grows outward by 8 stitches per RS row (2 yarn-overs at each of four corner markers). On WS rows all stitches are knitted (garter). The result is a square with diagonal lines running from the centre to each corner. Budget about 500 g (about 1,100 m / 1,200 yards) of DK wool.

content.text: 22 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over garter stitch on 4 mm needles, blocked. The square grows by 8 stitches per RS row; at gauge each RS row adds about 4.5 mm to the diagonal across the square. At 22 stitches per 10 cm, a 130 × 130 cm square requires approximately 286 RS rows and about 572 rows total.
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 8 stitches. Tail: allow approximately 20 cm. Place markers: after st 2, after st 4, after st 6. These divide the 8 cast-on stitches into 4 sections of 2 each.
RS row: *k to marker, yo, SM, yo; repeat from * 3 more times, k to end. (8 sts added per RS row)
Continue until the square measures 130 cm from corner to corner along one side (approximately 286 RS rows at gauge, giving 8 + (8 × 286) = 2,296 stitches).
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off across all stitches. At approximately 2,296 stitches this will take some time; use a long circular needle to hold all stitches comfortably.
After 50 RS rows: 8 + 400 = 408 stitches. Side length approximately 23 cm. The square corners are well defined.
After 150 RS rows: 1,208 stitches. Side length approximately 68 cm. Halfway to the finished size.

Square becomes a diamond (rhombus): all four corner yarn-overs were placed the same distance from each marker, so the four sections grew at exactly the same rate. This is correct for a diamond, not a square. For a square, two of the four corners must hold a yo-SM-yo sequence while the other two hold a yo-SM-k1-yo-SM sequence. If a square is the goal, ensure the corner markers sit at the exact midpoint of each edge, not at the corner points.

Edges rippling: the garter rows are slightly short relative to the increase rate at this gauge. Work every other RS row as a yo-only increase (omit the SM double-yo and work a single yo at alternate corners) to flatten the edge.
Soak in cool water, press out in towels. Pin the four corner points to the stated 130 × 130 cm dimensions. Pin along each edge between the corners. The square will lie very flat after blocking.
Hand wash in cool water, lay flat to dry. A large square shawl takes up to 48 hours to dry thoroughly at the centre.
Replace the plain garter body with a simple 4-row lace stripe every 20 rows. This creates a concentric pattern radiating from the centre, with the lace stripes marking the row count milestones.
